subject: Business Models
title: Data as Personal Property
description: A short lesson to help you apply Data as Personal Property.

hook.text: Your data generates $200/year for Google and Facebook combined. You get $0. Some want to change that.

buildup.text: Data ownership models propose that individuals should control and profit from their personal information.

discovery.text: Companies like Brave browser and Ocean Protocol pay users for their attention or data directly.

twist.text: GDPR gave Europeans data rights, but most click 'accept all cookies' anyway. Rights without behavior change little.

climax.text: If data ownership becomes law, the entire ad-tech industry—worth $600 billion—must restructure its business model.

punchline.text: $200/year of your data, $0 to you. Ownership could reshape a $600B industry.

quiz.question: What would happen if personal data ownership became standard?
options: The $600B ad-tech industry would need to restructure

details.summary: Data as personal property is the principle that individuals should own, control, and monetize the data they generate through digital activities..
details.whyItMatters: Personal data generates hundreds of billions in annual corporate revenue, yet individuals receive almost none of this value..
takeaways: Individuals would own and control the data they generate through digital activity
Emerging platforms let users sell their personal data directly to buyers
Data ownership could shift billions in value from corporations to individuals

faq.question: How much is an individual's personal data worth?
faq.answer: Estimates vary from $240 to $3,000 per person annually depending on demographic data, purchasing behavior, and data granularity. Facebook generates about $40 per US user per quarter in ad revenue from user data. The total personal data economy exceeds 200 billion dollars annually.

faq.question: What platforms allow individuals to monetize their own data?
faq.answer: Brave browser pays users in cryptocurrency for viewing ads. Datum and Ocean Protocol create marketplaces for personal data sales. Health data platforms like LunaDNA let users contribute genetic data for research compensation. These early examples remain small but demonstrate the emerging model.
